need: Agents named the task they had picked, or the tasks a piece of work waited on, by ID alone, such as a code and a stage number. A person reading the message could not tell what the work was without searching for the task's record.
evidence: The owner of one project reported this with an example message and asked for task names and links, then approved a proposal to require them and asked for the rule in the kit as well. An earlier draft of this lesson stated the rule in three procedures and added a command that prints a formatted reference; this version keeps one sentence and a pointer, because the title is already in the record the agent has read.
limits: The need was observed once, in one project. The source project's own change was written and not delivered, so no before and after exists, and the kit adds no check: nothing can read what an agent writes in a message. The source project does not install the kit, so this is a direct contribution rather than an installed-release export.
sanitization: Removed the project's task identifiers and titles, tool names, host names and paths. No credentials, private account data, employer, client or third-party material is included.
